data.title: INTEGRATED ATHLETE-PADDLE-HULL DYNAMICS IN FLATWATER SPRINT KAYAK FROM JOINT PATHOMECHANICS AND THE NEUROMUSCULAR ASYMPTOTE TO PARAMETRIC CUSTOM-TAILORED K1 HYDRODYNAMICS
data.title_original: INTEGRATED ATHLETE-PADDLE-HULL DYNAMICS IN FLATWATER SPRINT KAYAK FROM JOINT PATHOMECHANICS AND THE NEUROMUSCULAR ASYMPTOTE TO PARAMETRIC CUSTOM-TAILORED K1 HYDRODYNAMICS
data.summary: Abstract: Selecting the propulsive setup and hull configuration in elite flatwater sprint kayaking has historically relied on trial-and-error empiricism, rigid off-the-shelf catalog sizing (S, M, L, XL), and technical models that confuse extreme kinematic reach with hydrodynamic speed. This work establishes a closed systems-engineering model that unifies athlete physiology, lever mechanics, and Olympic K1 naval architecture. First, it analyzes the pathomechanics of repetitive joint injuries, showing how high paddle feather angles (60 degrees or higher) and excessive elbow drive force the wrist and shoulder into unnatural planes, precipitating tenosynovitis, rotator cuff impingement, and severe multi-axial stress on the lumbar spine. Second, the study calculates the unloaded neuromuscular ceiling of the human kinetic chain (190 to 210 strokes per minute at full movement range) and tracks its decay under hydrodynamic drag. It proves that downscaling from a traditional 780 cm² wing blade to a 750 cm² profile maintains equivalent forward propulsive impulse through a manageable cadence increase of 4 percent, while effectively eliminating hydro-biomechanical stall and stroke collapse under lactic acidosis. Third, by optimizing lever geometry—shifting the grip 5 cm closer to the paddle collar and shortening the shaft to 203 cm—the setup reduces joint resistive torque at the catch by over 10 to 15 percent. This shorter, more vertical paddle orientation suppresses downward vertical pitch forces by 9.5 percent and dampens lateral yaw snaking by nearly 8 percent, lowering overall hull resistance by 1.1 percent. These hydro-mechanical gains translate into estimated competitive advantages of 0.13 seconds over 200 m, 0.35 seconds over 500 m, and 0.75 seconds over 1000 m. Finally, the paper demonstrates how rapid Large-Format Additive Manufacturing (LFAM) with carbon-reinforced thermoplastics eliminates the economic dependence on fixed industrial molds. This enables the production of custom-tailored K1 hulls engineered to match each athlete's dynamic center of gravity, metacentric stability, and individual stroke clearance corridor, delivering a race-ready boat in just seven to ten days.

data.title: Репрезентация техники движений античных атлетов по изображениям древнегреческой вазописи
data.title_original: Репрезентация техники движений античных атлетов по изображениям древнегреческой вазописи
data.summary: На примерах пяти современных олимпийских легкоатлетических дисциплин проанализирована техника древнегреческих атлетов в сравнении с современными спортсменами. Сравнение проводилось с точки зрения эффективности пространственно-временных и динамических характеристик движений. Для оценивания использовались доступные античные артефакты, такие как изображения на древнегреческих амфорах и других сосудах, античная статуя дискобола, а также свидетельства древнегреческих историков. Проведенное исследование показало высокую степень понимания жителями Античной Греции основных анатомических и биомеханических принципов двигательных действий.

data.title: Characteristics of patients receiving a prescription for adapted physical activity in Aubervilliers: a retrospective study
data.title_original: Characteristics of patients receiving a prescription for adapted physical activity in Aubervilliers: a retrospective study
data.summary: physical activity identified in the study was the desire for good mental, physical, and social health¹⁰. Due to its sustainable nature, this program, a pioneer in France since 2015, seemed conducive to studying adherence to an adapted physical activity program.The main objective of the study was to describe the sociodemographic profile of patients benefiting from this program since its creation in 2015. The secondary objective was to compare the profile of patients who received an APA prescription under this program but never attended any session with those who attended multiple sessions.METHOD Study Type and PopulationA retrospective observational study was conducted. The study population consisted of adult patients who consulted at the Aubervilliers CMS and who had received a prescription under the "exercise on prescription" program.The city of Aubervilliers is in Seine-Saint-Denis (93), a department with an over-representation of cardiovascular diseases and social precarity¹¹. The "exercise on prescription" program was created in 2015 at the Aubervilliers CMS in partnership with the municipality. It is free for beneficiaries. Initially, the GP identifies the indication, proposes it to the patient, and prescribes it. The prescribing physicians for APA could be GPs from the CMS and some private GPs in Aubervilliers who were partners in the program. The patient is then registered, and the contact details of the sports educator are provided to them. The sports educator has validated training as a level 2 health-sport animator from the Île-de-France Regional Olympic and Sports Center. They offer an interview during which they assess the patient's functional abilities, then specify the modalities of the APA sessions, with the possibility of attending one or more weekly sessions, with multiple time slots during the week and several activities (yoga, muscle strengthening, aquagym). The number of sessions is not predetermined and depends on the participant. Data Collection Methods All patients who received an APA prescription from a GP practicing at the Aubervilliers CMS since the creation of the program were included in the study, regardless of whether they resided in Aubervilliers. data.title: Sports Policy and National Development: A Comparative Study of India & China
data.title_original: Sports Policy and National Development: A Comparative Study of India & China
data.summary: Sports, we now know, are not just a form of entertainment or physical activity; they are also linked to health, education, social inclusion, economic development, youth empowerment and the global identity of a country. Sports are a major part of India and China's national development agendas, yet the sports policies of India and China have a different structure, priority and approach. China has achieved a lot of success in elite competitive sports with a centralized and goal-oriented system. In recent years, India has focused more on the mass movement of sports, talent identification and sports infrastructure, the participation of women and differently-abled athletes, and international excellence. The Khelo Bharat Niti-2025 has been introduced by India on 10 July 2025. It is aimed at a more inclusive sports ecosystem from the grassroots to the Olympic stage. It is all about talent identification, sports science, sports medicine, sports infrastructure, social inclusion and sports as a career. Sports policy is in its first phase in China now with a vision of becoming a "Sports power" nation. China's "Plan for Building a Sports Power during the 15th Five-Year Period," published in 2026, focuses on public health, sports competition quality, sports governance and the development of the sports sector. In this research paper we compare the sports policies of both countries in terms of similarities, differences and achievements, and potential lessons for India.

data.title: Disclosure, Concealment, and Accountable Testimony: A 20-Year Comparative Textual Analysis of Islamic Moral Reasoning in a Muslim Athlete's Autoethnographies
data.title_original: Disclosure, Concealment, and Accountable Testimony: A 20-Year Comparative Textual Analysis of Islamic Moral Reasoning in a Muslim Athlete's Autoethnographies
data.summary: Autoethnography can connect embodied experience to the social organisation of sport, but writing the self also exposes relationships, institutions, and other people. Relational ethics addresses this problem, yet sport scholarship has given comparatively less attention to the explicit moral traditions through which authors decide both what to disclose and what to withhold. This article conducts a critical autoethnographic textual comparison of two works written twenty years apart. The first is a 2006 doctoral study of power, coercion, injury, and the coach-athlete relationship. The second is a 2026 book that locates sporting development within a broader life history and the Maldives’ inaugural Olympic participation. 16 focal representational decisions were analysed through a comparison matrix and five situated Islamic concepts: amanah (trust), 'adl (justice), niyyah (intention), satr (protective concealment), and hisab (accountability). The comparison shows a shift from an individuated pseudonym carrying diary-derived speech towards named individuals, selective paraphrase, recurrent retrospective self-correction, and wider structural framing. Both texts declare reconstruction rather than transcription, so what changes across the twenty years is the unit of representation rather than the evidential claim. From this analysis, the article develops accountable testimony: a non-mechanical approach that places a burden of justification on silence as well as disclosure. It contributes to autoethnographic ethics and athlete safeguarding by showing how faith-informed moral reasoning can be made methodologically explicit, proportionate, and open to scholarly scrutiny.

data.title: Biomechanics of the Snatch and Clean and Jerk in Olympic Weightlifting: A Systematic Review
data.title_original: Biomechanics of the Snatch and Clean and Jerk in Olympic Weightlifting: A Systematic Review
data.summary: Biomechanical studies of the Olympic snatch and clean and jerk use heterogeneous samples and measurement protocols. This systematic review summarizes measurement approaches, technical findings, lift-specific coverage, and sex representation. Web of Science Core Collection, PubMed and Scopus were searched on 20 September 2026, retaining publications first available by 30 June 2026. The exports contained 241, 151 and 264 records (656 in total); 314 duplicate entries were removed, leaving 342 distinct database records. The authors confirmed full-text assessment of the previously assembled evidence set. Of its 74 publications, one narrative review (Bartonietz, 1996) was reclassified as contextual rather than original research, leaving 73 primary publications. Fifty-two of the original 74 entries matched the new electronic exports by DOI or title; 21 additional primary publications were retained from the authors’ previously assembled reference set. Among the 73 primary publications, 45 examined the snatch only, 15 examined clean/jerk movements without snatch data, and 13 examined both categories; 23 included female athletes. Eight publications are cited only for methodological or contextual interpretation. Heterogeneity precluded meta-analysis. The review highlights the uneven coverage of the competition lifts, limited female representation and need for comparable, field-validated multimodal measurements. No prospective review protocol was registered.

data.title: A Snow Sports Venue Low-Carbon Evaluation System Based on Life-Cycle Carbon Emissions
data.title_original: A Snow Sports Venue Low-Carbon Evaluation System Based on Life-Cycle Carbon Emissions
data.summary: Large-scale snow sports venues are characterized by unique terrain, seasonal operation modes, and long service lifespan. Consequently, a comprehensive assessment method is required to account for both life-cycle carbon emissions and multi-dimensional low-carbon performance. This study proposes a Sports Venue Low-carbon Evaluation System (SV-LCES) that integrates life-cycle carbon emission evaluation (LCCE) with multidimensional performance assessment. Using engineering inventories, EnergyPlus simulations, and emission factor methods, a life-cycle carbon emission model was developed and applied to the National Sliding Centre (NSC) and Yanqing Winter Olympic Village (YWOV), with the latter constructed as a supporting venue for the NSC. Carbon hotspots were identified, and an evaluation system was established through the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) and LCCE combined weighting and grey clustering. The results show that the operation and maintenance stage was the dominant contributor to the life-cycle carbon emissions, accounting for 56.39% of the total. The calculated carbon emission reduction rates of the NSC and YWOV were 40.17% and 46.37%, respectively, indicating a relatively small difference. However, after the low-carbon performance of the venues was comprehensively evaluated, SV-LCES distinguished their performance levels as Grade B for NSC and Grade A for YWOV. The proposed framework offers a holistic approach to low-carbon evaluation of large-scale sports venues and other energy-intensive public buildings.

data.title: Strategic Application of Post-exercise Cold-Water Immersion to Enhance Performance Recovery and Adaptation: An Umbrella Review of 15 Published Systematic Reviews with Meta-analysis
data.title_original: Strategic Application of Post-exercise Cold-Water Immersion to Enhance Performance Recovery and Adaptation: An Umbrella Review of 15 Published Systematic Reviews with Meta-analysis
data.summary: BACKGROUND: Athletes commonly implement post-exercise cold-water immersion (CWI), with several meta-analyses having assessed its effectiveness. OBJECTIVES: To thoroughly review, appraise, and summarise existing systematic reviews with meta-analyses (SRMA) examining the effects of post-exercise CWI on the recovery of exercise performance and adaptation. METHODS: An umbrella review was conducted in accordance with the Joanna Briggs Institute guidelines. Methodological quality was assessed using AMSTAR 2, and certainty of evidence using GRADE. PROSPERO registration: (CRD420251103267). Eight databases were searched, including Web of Science, Scopus, SPORTDiscus, CINAHL, Cochrane Library, Embase, MEDLINE, and PubMed. Systematic reviews with meta-analyses of peer-reviewed randomised controlled trials examining post-exercise CWI vs passive rest or other recovery modalities on performance, training adaptation, or physiological, biochemical, and perceptual outcomes in healthy humans were included, with restriction to the English language. RESULTS: Fifteen SRMAs published between 2011 and 2025, comprising 161 unique studies, were included. Overall methodological quality was low to critically low, and certainty of evidence was low to very low, mainly due to inconsistency and imprecision. Protocols of 10-15 min at 10-15 or 5-10 °C appear to be most effective for improving performance and recovery. Post-exercise CWI resulted in significant improvements in muscular power at 24 h post-high-intensity exercise and at 24-48 h post-eccentric exercise, and in jump performance at 24-48 h, despite impaired jump performance in the initial hours after post-exercise CWI. Endurance performance improved immediately after CWI, but CWI produced no later benefits or positive effects on adaptations. CWI did not improve muscular strength performance, and impaired strength and hypertrophic gains. CWI improved heart rate variability immediately after exercise, reduced muscle soreness up to 96 h, and lowered creatine kinase (CK) concentrations between 24 and 72 h, with no significant effects on C-reactive protein or interleukin-6 up to 72 h. No immediate impact on blood lactate or lactate dehydrogenase was found, although some reductions appear 24-72 h post-exercise. CONCLUSIONS: Post-exercise CWI confers outcome-specific recovery benefits but may impair resistance training adaptations with chronic use. These findings support a periodised, context-driven approach to CWI implementation rather than routine application after all exercise sessions.

data.title: Sporting Ambitions, Geopolitical Goals
data.title_original: Sporting Ambitions, Geopolitical Goals
data.summary: This chapter will cover Morocco’s engagement with international sport. The focus will be on how this country leverages sports events to advance its geopolitical, economic and cultural objectives. Morocco showcases its organisational capabilities and infrastructure by hosting prestigious events at the regional and global level, positioning itself as a relevant player in global sports governance. In particular, football serves as a cornerstone of Morocco’s sports diplomacy, highlighting its role as co-host (alongside Spain and Portugal) of the 2030 FIFA Men’s World Cup, its historic fourth place in 2022 and the men’s bronze medal in the Paris 2024 Olympics. These achievements, together with the development of scouting processes leading to the naturalisation of athletes from the diasporas, have amplified the national pride and elevated the country’s global visibility. A challenge for Moroccan sports diplomacy is the management of internal, regional and international political tensions, especially concerning Western Sahara, which has caused some sporting incidents with Algeria and Spain. Therefore, Morocco illuminates how African nations can globally use sports as a tool for soft power, geopolitical manoeuvring and the assertion of national identity.

data.title: Stable technical profile despite increasing technical diversity across the last three Olympic cycles in elite female extra-lightweight judo
data.title_original: Stable technical profile despite increasing technical diversity across the last three Olympic cycles in elite female extra-lightweight judo
data.summary: Objective: To analyze the technical-tactical behavior and scoring effectiveness of techniques in elite female extra-lightweight (≤48 kg) judo across the last three Olympic cycles (2016, 2020, and 2024). Methods: A retrospective observational study which analyzed 159 official International Judo Federation World Circuit contests (53 per cycle) involving athletes ranked among the top 20 in the World Ranking. A total of 107 scoring techniques were identified according to the Kodokan classification and the official IJF rules applicable to each Olympic cycle. Results: No significant differences were observed in the distribution of technical groups across Olympic cycles (χ²=3.109, p=0.927; Cramér's V=0.121). Likewise, the distribution of techniques resulting in Ippon (χ²=3.637, p=0.888) and Waza-ari (χ²=6.383, p=0.604) remained stable. Although the overall technical profile was preserved, the diversity of individual scoring techniques increased from 17 techniques in the 2016 Olympic cycle to 24 in the 2020 cycle, and remained high in 2024 (23 techniques). Sode-tsuri-komi-goshi predominated in 2016, whereas Ouchi-gari became the most frequent scoring technique in 2020 and remained among the leading techniques in 2024. Katame-waza consistently produced most Ippon, whereas Ashi-waza and Te-waza remained the principal sources of Waza-ari. Conclusions: Despite successive IJF rule modifications, the technical profile of elite female extra-lightweight judo remained remarkably stable across the last three Olympic cycles. Elite athletes expanded their technical repertoire while maintaining the effectiveness of the principal scoring strategies, providing coaches with evidence to optimize weight category-specific technical and tactical training.

data.title: National Pride vs. Global Unity: Exploring Nationalism-Infused CSR and Stakeholder Perceptions in Global Sports Events
data.title_original: National Pride vs. Global Unity: Exploring Nationalism-Infused CSR and Stakeholder Perceptions in Global Sports Events
data.summary: Abstract Global sporting events, such as the Olympics, often highlight a delicate tension between universal ideals of corporate social responsibility (CSR) and nationalistic appeals to local pride. Against this backdrop, the present study investigates how moral foundations (fairness vs. loyalty) and national attachment shape stakeholder perceptions of nationalism-infused CSR motives and CSR authenticity. Building on moral foundation theory and attribution-based CSR research, we tested hypotheses regarding the interplay between these variables. Conducting a survey (N = 755) through Dynata, we found that fairness-oriented individuals attributed egoistic- and strategic-driven motives, while people with in-group/loyalty foundation perceived value-driven motives from the initiatives.

data.title: Illuminating Olympicenes: Insights Into Anti‐Kasha Photophysics in Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbons
data.title_original: Illuminating Olympicenes: Insights Into Anti‐Kasha Photophysics in Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbons
data.summary: ABSTRACT Olympicene, or 6 H ‐benzo[ cd ]pyrene, is a polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) with five fused six‐membered rings arranged in a pattern reminiscent of the Olympic symbol. While functionalized olympicene‐based materials have captivated attention for their unique graphene‐fragment topology and aromaticity, their photoluminescent properties remain virtually unexplored. Here, we synthesize olympicene‐core functionalized derivatives and report their “anomalous” photophysical properties. These olympicene derivatives display extensive vibronic structure and highly interacting electronic states. Such effects give rise to excited‐state dynamics that are rare and unconventional in small PAH systems. Specifically, these olympicene derivatives exhibit dual fluorescence upon photoexcitation, accompanied by pronounced excitation‐dependent emission behavior. Spectroscopic evidence demonstrates these behaviors arise from multiple singlet emissive states—an anti‐Kasha locally excited (LE) state ( S n , n ≥ 2) and an intramolecular charge transfer (ICT) state. This work positions olympicene‐functionalized derivatives as a new platform to study fundamental photophysics. Exploring these properties will lead to new and advanced optoelectronic applications.

data.title: Uma investigação da matriz ética e moral desportiva
data.title_original: Uma investigação da matriz ética e moral desportiva
data.summary: This work, which is philosophical in nature and focuses on the field of sports, aims to conduct transdisciplinary research on ethical principles and the formation of the moral foundation of sports. Thus, through a literature review on the subject, it discusses historical concepts and studies of morality and the human ethical framework as the foundation and driving force of the evolutionary process. Thus, it highlights the schools of thought that have influenced modern sporting ideology and normative and educational practices, such as the Olympic tradition of fair play and its benefits for moral education. As a result of the study, concepts were identified that support the initial hypothesis and provide a scientific basis for research into the roots of sports ethics and morality.

data.title: Transforming India’s Sports Ecosystem for Global Sporting Excellence
data.title_original: Transforming India’s Sports Ecosystem for Global Sporting Excellence
data.summary: In today’s world, sports are no longer just an entertainment medium or physical activity but have become a powerful tool for Health, Educational Development, Employment Generation, and Social Inclusion, National Pride, Economic Progress, and Youth Empowerment. It has thus been necessary for India, being a large and young country, to create a sound, inclusive, and sustainable sports ecosystem. A sports ecosystem refers to a linked system in which various factors such as sports infrastructure, talent detection, coaching, sports science, medicine, education, competitions, finance, and employment come together to form a whole. Though there is no dearth of sports talent in India, what is missing is an effective system for talent identification, cultivation, and elevation to the international level. Khelo India, Fit India, and the Olympic Podium Scheme are some of the steps taken in this direction. Khelo Bharat Niti-2025, launched in this year, stresses the need for connecting sports to national building, economic growth, social development, and mass movement. This article discusses the importance of creating a strong sports ecosystem in India, its current situation, the main challenges it is facing, the opportunities and ways for developing it. It concludes that a holistic sports system from grassroots sports to elite sports is necessary for India, instead of focusing only on winning medals.

data.title: Olympic-patterned pentaboron emitter featuring highly distorted geometry enables efficient solution-processed ultrapure green OLEDs
data.title_original: Olympic-patterned pentaboron emitter featuring highly distorted geometry enables efficient solution-processed ultrapure green OLEDs
data.summary: Efficient, ultrapure green organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs) fabricated via wet processing are crucial for ultrahigh definition displays but remain highly challenging due to the paucity of suitable emitters. Herein, we developed Oly-BN, a novel multipleresonance thermally activated delayed fluorescence (MR-TADF) emitter featuring a distinct Olympic-patterned boron-distribution. The zigzag doped heteroatom polycyclic aromatic framework enables near-degenerate singlet/triplet excited states. Integrating para-N-π-B motifs helps regulate the triplet manifold and emission color point, enabling energetically accessible higher lying triplet excited states with enhanced spinorbit coupling, while also suppressing low-frequency structural relaxation and modulating the optical bandgap. Oly-BN in toluene exhibits vivid green emission at 522 nm with a narrow full width at half maximum (FWHM) of 17 nm, a photoluminescence quantum yield of 95%, and a fast reverse intersystem crossing rate constant of 6.9×106 s−1. Additionally, its highly twisted conformation weakens intermolecular interactions and favors bright, solid-state emission. The nonsensitized solution-processed OLEDs deliver ultrapure green electroluminescence with a CIEy value up to 0.73, and achieves an optimized maximum external quantum efficiency of 39.4%, which remains high at 29.9% at 1000 cd m-2. This work not only provides a promising highly saturated green emitter for solution-processed OLEDs but also demonstrates the importance of precisely integrating heteroatoms in modulating photophysical properties of MR-TADF emitters.

data.title: Historiographical dimensions of Ukrainian physical culture and sport: a bibliometric analysis of the global scholarly discourse (1991–2025)
data.title_original: Historiographical dimensions of Ukrainian physical culture and sport: a bibliometric analysis of the global scholarly discourse (1991–2025)
data.summary: The article analyses the scholarly discourse on the history of the system of physical education, sport and physical activity in Ukraine in contemporary periodicals. Background and aim of the study. The globalisation of science makes it necessary to examine how the Ukrainian past is reflected in international scholarly works, which is essential for overcoming the sense of inferiority and for decolonising national history. Despite the existence of individual reviews, a comprehensive analysis of international publications is still lacking, and researchers have not yet clarified the specific features of how the history of Ukrainian sport and physical culture is being integrated into the global academic space. The aim of the study is to substantiate, on the basis of an analysis of an international body of publications (Scopus, Web of Science, Google Scholar, 1991–2025), the distinctive nature of the Ukrainian history of physical culture and sport as a sociocultural phenomenon and to identify the main thematic areas of its current research. Material and methods. Using bibliometric and comparative analysis methods, a representative body of publications (1991–2025) was examined. The structural and systemic approach made it possible to classify and organise this body of documents according to key thematic clusters. Results. The quantitative analysis revealed a growth in the number of publications (up to 7.6 works per year in 2016–2025), with periodicals (89%) and foreign authors (64%) predominating. Qualitative content analysis made it possible to identify five key thematic areas: physical culture and sport as an ideological and political instrument (using the example of the Soviet system and current sports sanctions); the role of national forms of physical activity and body practices (Sokil, Plast, Fighting Hopak) in shaping identity; the development of sport in the context of modernisation processes and urban history; the evolution of health-enhancing and recreational physical culture, from the therapeutic gymnastics of the early 20th century to the modern fitness industry; and the grassroots self-organisation of physical culture and sports societies. Conclusions. The analysis showed an interdisciplinary and internationally oriented renewal of Ukrainian historiography of physical culture and sport. Overcoming the identified chronological and regional imbalances through methodological modernisation is a promising direction for future global research.

data.title: Dynamics of the Competitiveness of Russian Male and Female Pole Vaulters During the 2020–2024 Olympic Cycle
data.title_original: Dynamics of the Competitiveness of Russian Male and Female Pole Vaulters During the 2020–2024 Olympic Cycle
data.summary: The level of competitiveness in pole vaulting reflects not only athletic performance but also the effectiveness of athlete development within the discipline. This study examines changes in the competitive dynamics of Russian male and female pole vaulters during the 2020–2024 Olympic cycle and identifies factors associated with these changes. The analysis was based on official results from the Russian Indoor and Outdoor Athletics Championships. Competitive dynamics were assessed using a combination of literature review, comparative analysis of competition results, calculation of competitiveness coefficients, statistical analysis, and expert consultations with experienced pole vault specialists. The results indicate a gradual decline in competitiveness in the women’s event, accompanied by lower performance density and a widening gap between leading athletes and the remainder of the field. In contrast, the men’s event demonstrated relatively stable competitive characteristics throughout the study period. These findings provide an empirical assessment of the current state of the discipline and may contribute to improving long-term athlete development, optimizing competition planning, and monitoring the effectiveness of pole vault development programmes.

data.title: The Ubiquitous Role of the Smartphone in Breaking: An Ethnographic-Informed Study
data.title_original: The Ubiquitous Role of the Smartphone in Breaking: An Ethnographic-Informed Study
data.summary: Breaking is a physically demanding street dance, which is highly creative and historically rooted in urban culture. Studies about Breaking are scant, and the role of technology in the modality, e.g., smartphones, while potentially relevant according to a previous technology review, is still unknown. This study is a first step into understanding the role of technology in Breaking. Drawing on observations of 35 training sessions and 15 interviews with Non-Professional to Olympic-level Breakers, we found that smartphones act as digital scaffolds for Breaking. Smartphone use supports training structure, movement arsenal management, performance improvement and creativity, and peer feedback and community engagement. Our contribution is two-fold: we first contribute a detailed understanding of how smartphones mediate Breaking, a form of appropriating the smartphone which has not been previously described; then, we outline design opportunities for future systems aimed at Breaking and other modalities, which are non-hierarchical, heavily rooted in culture, and turn to peer-to-peer expertise exchange to develop complex physical practices.

data.title: The ımpact of visual attention and visual memory exercises on athletes’ ımagery skills
data.title_original: The ımpact of visual attention and visual memory exercises on athletes’ ımagery skills
data.summary: Background and Study Aim. Imagery has increasingly gained attention as a mental training technique in the field of sport psychology. Many Olympic and elite athletes effectively employ imagery training to enhance their performance. Although a substantial body of research has demonstrated the positive effects of imagery training on athletic performance, further research is still needed to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of these interventions. In this context, the present study aims to examine the effects of visual attention and visual memory exercises on athletes’ imagery abilities. Method: A total of 30 athletes participated in this study; 15 were assigned to the experimental group and 15 to the control group. The participants were selected from university team athletes competing in basketball, football, and volleyball. The study was conducted using a quasi-experimental design within the framework of quantitative research methods. Data were collected using the Movement Imagery Questionnaire, the d2 Test of Attention, and the n-back test. A repeated measures ANOVA was conducted to examine time-dependent changes between the experimental and control groups. Results: The findings indicate that the six-week visual attention and visual memory training program did not have a significant effect on athletes’ visual attention skills; however, it led to improvements in their visual memory abilities. Furthermore, analyses conducted in the second phase of the study revealed that, in line with improvements in visual memory, athletes also demonstrated enhanced imagery abilities. Conclusion: The results suggest that the implemented visual memory exercises significantly improved athletes’ visual memory performance, and that this improvement was associated with notable enhancements in both kinesthetic and visual imagery abilities. In contrast, the visual attention exercises did not produce a statistically significant effect on attention performance. Overall, visual memory appears to play a central role in the cognitive foundations of imagery ability.

data.title: Integration of Artificial Intelligence in Olympic Security and it's Challenges
data.title_original: Integration of Artificial Intelligence in Olympic Security and it's Challenges
data.summary: The modern wave of terrorist violence has also cast its shadow on the Olympics. The world&s;s biggest sporting event provides terrorist groups with a perfect platform to gain attention and create a sense of fear across countries. In the post 9/11 world, security measures have been enhanced due to the perception of heightened threat of terrorist violence. At least since the 2004 Athens Olympics, technological solutions are being explored and integrated to enhance the security of the games. China was the first country to use Artificial Intelligence for security purposes at the summer Olympics in 2008. Since then, each host country has invested significant resources in securing the games. These measures have not just increased the costs of hosting Olympics, but security related budget now constitute a significant part of the overall Olympics spending. The security and surveillance systems deployed and tested at Olympics are among its lasting legacies especially for authoritarian regimes. The reliability of the AI tools used is another challenge. States hosting must contemplate these choices when they organising the Olympics.

data.title: PARQUE RADICAL DE DEODORO – RIO DE JANEIRO: Características, usos no período pós-jogos e necessidades da comunidade local
data.title_original: PARQUE RADICAL DE DEODORO – RIO DE JANEIRO: Características, usos no período pós-jogos e necessidades da comunidade local
data.summary: This paper aims to investigate the characteristics of Olympic facilities, their use in the post-games period, and the needs of the local community. The research is justified by the recurring underutilization of Olympic facilities, which raises questions about urban planning and social inclusion. To meet the objective, the study was conducted at the facilities of Parque Radical, Deodoro Sports Complex, Rio de Janeiro. Questionnaires were applied to 132 users of the Deodoro Sports Complex and 108 residents of the surrounding area. In addition, 55 interviews were conducted with users of the Deodoro Sports Complex, residents of the surrounding area, and employees of Parque Radical. Quantitative data from the questionnaires were analyzed using SPSS/PC software, while the interviews were interpreted qualitatively. The results indicate that adapting the facilities for multiple uses favors access to sports and leisure, but operational barriers limit their use. The location in a vulnerable area did not guarantee integration with the community, highlighting the need for public policies to enable their continued use. The study contributes to the debate on Olympic legacies and suggests strategies to make these spaces more accessible and sustainable.

data.title: Virginia Woolf: dance, rhythm, movement
data.title_original: Virginia Woolf: dance, rhythm, movement
data.summary: Despite the rich cultural exchange between the arts in the late-nineteenth and early twentieth centuries, particularly between dance and literature, the study of rhythm, movement, and dance has been relatively neglected in Woolf studies. Moving beyond the current critical focus on ballet, this thesis draws on Virginia Woolf’s biographies, diaries, essays, juvenilia, letters, and novels, alongside the socio-cultural history of dance and feminist theories of the body and gendered movement, to explore how Woolf’s use of physical expression, dance, and rhythmic variation might upend orthodox masculinity, patriarchal oppression, and social class hierarchies. Chapter one looks at how Woolf employs circle- or couple-dances in The Voyage Out (1915) to explore embodiment, gender fluidity, and social control. Formally staid ballroom dance, regarded as a manifestation of patriarchy, is replaced with vibrant Bacchanalian movements that mirror modern dance’s focus on spontaneous, voluntary motion. Chapter two argues that Orlando’s ballet-inflected steps test the limits of conservative masculinity, embracing alternative forms. It goes on to consider the figure of the female Olympic ice-dancer as a possible source of inspiration for Princess Sasha Romanovich, whose fluid movement across the ice resists conformity. Chapter three delves into human/nonhuman dance-related movement in Flush: A Biography (1933), To the Lighthouse (1927) and The Waves (1931), examining how ingenious female artists breach gender boundaries by operating outside male-dominated models. Consequently, Woolf’s engagement with the nonhuman is less concerned with destabilising humanist values than with deepening her critique of gender inequality. The final chapter investigates how the foxtrot and embodied movement in The Years and Between the Acts (1941) critique social hierarchies, reflecting the novelist’s democratic response to elitism. As such, this thesis intervenes in, and contributes to, various debates in Woolf studies, offering fresh insights into Virginia Woolf’s engagement with embodiment, gender, and social politics.

data.title: Ergogenic effects of beetroot juice supplementation on neuromuscular function and simulated combat demands in elite female taekwondo athletes
data.title_original: Ergogenic effects of beetroot juice supplementation on neuromuscular function and simulated combat demands in elite female taekwondo athletes
data.summary: Beetroot juice supplementation has been widely examined across various sport disciplines due to its potential ergogenic effects. However, evidence regarding its impact on combat sports particularly in female athletes remains limited. The aim of this study was to evaluate the acute effects of beetroot juice supplementation on simulated taekwondo combat performance and neuromuscular function in elite female taekwondo athletes. Seven elite female Olympic taekwondo athletes (age: 20.3 ± 3.7 years), participated in a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study consisting of two experimental trials). Each trial involved the consumption of either 140 mL of beetroot juice (which contains 12.8 mmol NO₃⁻) or 140 mL of a placebo (with 0.08 mmol NO₃⁻) followed by a simulated taekwondo combat session and assessments of neuro-muscular function (i.e., vertical jump and visual cognitive performance). In addition, metabolic (i.e., blood lactate), and perceptual responses (i.e., rate of perceived exertion) were measured before, after, and 3 minutes post-combat. No significant differences during the simulated taekwondo combat (e.g., attack time; p = 0.531–0.989; ηp² = 0.01–0.05), neuromuscular function battery (p = 0.302-0.700; ηp² = 0.02-0.04), blood lactate concentrations (p = 0.705; ηp² = 0.13), or rate of perceived exertion values (RPE) (p = 0.717; ηp² = 0.12) were obtained between beetroot juice and placebo conditions. Acute ingestion of beetroot juice (140 mL) did not enhance simulated combat performance or neuromuscular function in female Olympic taekwondo athletes.

data.title: “The gym became a bit of a lab”: International Olympic Weightlifting coaches’ situated knowledges of training women athletes
data.title_original: “The gym became a bit of a lab”: International Olympic Weightlifting coaches’ situated knowledges of training women athletes
data.summary: In this paper, we extend gender-responsive coaching literature by examining how coaches’ learning processes influence their knowledges about sex, gender and athleticism. Our analysis draws upon semi-structured interviews with 10 coaches of elite women Olympic Weightlifters from eight countries: Aotearoa New Zealand, Botswana, Canada, China, Colombia, Denmark, the Philippines and the United States. Using Haraway’s concept of “situated knowledge”, we discuss how coaches’ knowledges were shaped by their national sport systems, gender norms within their national contexts, and their bodily experiences of Olympic Weightlifting. Exploring the contradictory understandings of women’s bodies, minds and motivations that these coaches relayed, we discuss whether any of these knowledges can be considered “better” than the others. We conclude that while coaches’ contradictory knowledges may be constructed in response to the diverse gendered bodies and identities that they encounter, they may still be critiqued based on the futures they imply for women athletes.

data.title: Editorial: Exploring the multidisciplinary roles of sports events
data.title_original: Editorial: Exploring the multidisciplinary roles of sports events
data.summary: The five core pillars of this topic, drawing on original empirical research and systematic reviews, illustrate the multidisciplinary complexity of the sporting landscape, namely:  The success of major sports events is fundamentally dependent on the volunteer workforce, a vital human resource that facilitates long-term social legacies. Empirical evidence from the Special Olympics World Games 2023 (SOWG 23) reveals that volunteer motivations in inclusive settings are primarily intrinsic, driven by a desire to express personal values and establish interpersonal contacts.Notably, the research identifies a parental history of volunteering as a key predictor of sustained engagement, suggesting that values instilled during childhood continue to influence active commitment well into adulthood. For sports organisations, these findings underscore the importance of shifting the recruitment focus away from extrinsic rewards toward strategies that emphasise community building and value alignment. To ensure a sustainable volunteering legacy, managers must implement di erentiated communication channels, such as digital platforms tailored to younger generations, to foster lasting engagement across diverse demographic groups. The multidisciplinary nature of sports events is also evident in how di erent stakeholders perceive quality. The case of GIMNASTRADA 2019, an international recreational gymnastics event, uses Service Quality Theory and Role Theory to demonstrate that "success" is highly subjective. The study found that the type of participation significantly influences quality ratings: while organisers and group leaders reported the highest levels of satisfaction, active gymnasts tended to have lower perceptions of service quality. This discrepancy is attributed to the "expectation-performance gap," in which active participants face greater performance pressure and have more stringent requirements for facilities and logistics. These findings suggest that sports management must move toward a tailored experience design, ensuring that the specific needs of athletes, families, and spectators are addressed separately to promote long-term loyalty and repeat participation. Sports events also serve as a "cultural battlefield" where national identity is constructed and contested. An analysis of Indonesian media narratives regarding the naturalisation of football players illustrates the tension between pragmatic nationalism and cultural essentialism. Media outlets often frame naturalised players as "national assets" who enhance international competitiveness, yet they simultaneously express scepticism about the athletes' "authenticity" and emotional ties to the nation. Drawing on the distinction between "thin citizenship" (legal recognition) and "thick citizenship" (cultural intimacy), the research shows how the media acts as a mediator of public perception. While some naturalised athletes successfully integrate by embracing local language and social initiatives, the discourse remains divided. This highlights the role of sporting events as critical sites for defining the symbolic boundaries of an "imagined community" in the era of globalised labour migration. From an economic and marketing perspective, the success of sports events is often linked to the "fit" or congruity between the event and its sponsoring brands. A metaanalytic review of 31 studies confirms that high levels of sports event-brand fit lead to positive cognitive, emotional, and behavioural responses from consumers. However, the e ectiveness of this fit is moderated by cultural contexts. In Eastern cultures, brand-event alignment is more e ective at generating emotional responses, reflecting a preference for harmony and collectivism. Conversely, in Western cultures, the fit has a stronger impact on behavioural intentions, such as purchase probability. Furthermore, the research suggests that symbolic brand responses-such as brand loyalty-are not instantaneous but require long-term sponsorship commitment and repeated interaction to bridge the "expectation gap" in consumers' minds. The final multidisciplinary lens focuses on the impact and legacy of sports events on the Quality of Life (QOL) of host communities. A scoping review of the literature indicates a significant shift from evaluating purely economic outcomes to measuring subjective well-being. While mega-events like the Olympics dominate the research, the review identifies an underexplored potential in small and mediumsized events to foster social capital and community cohesion. The findings suggest that the positive "feel-good" e ect of one-o mega-events is often temporary. In contrast, recurring participatory events (such as marathons) may o er more sustainable benefits for resident attachment and behavioural change. To advance this field, researchers advocate integrating objective measures, such as Heart Rate Variability (HRV), to complement subjective surveys and better understand the physiological mechanisms linking sports experiences to societal happiness.In conclusion, the articles in Exploring the Multidisciplinary Roles of Sports Events o er a profound and critical perspective on the role of sport in contemporary society. Collectively, they provide academics, event managers, and policymakers with practical insights and actionable tools to maximise the social legacies of sports events by understanding the intergenerational dynamics of volunteer motivation, improve service delivery through greater recognition of the role-specific expectations of diverse event participants, navigate the complex identity politics surrounding sports journalism and national team recruitment, optimise sponsorship strategies by acknowledging cultural di erences in consumer behaviour, and promote long-term societal well-being by moving beyond short-term economic metrics towards more holistic quality-of-life indicators. Taken together, the findings presented in this volume constitute a significant contribution to the ongoing dialogue on how sports events can be strategically leveraged to foster more inclusive, prosperous, and happier societies.

data.summary_original: The five core pillars of this topic, drawing on original empirical research and systematic reviews, illustrate the multidisciplinary complexity of the sporting landscape, namely:  The success of major sports events is fundamentally dependent on the volunteer workforce, a vital human resource that facilitates long-term social legacies. Empirical evidence from the Special Olympics World Games 2023 (SOWG 23) reveals that volunteer motivations in inclusive settings are primarily intrinsic, driven by a desire to express personal values and establish interpersonal contacts.Notably, the research identifies a parental history of volunteering as a key predictor of sustained engagement, suggesting that values instilled during childhood continue to influence active commitment well into adulthood. For sports organisations, these findings underscore the importance of shifting the recruitment focus away from extrinsic rewards toward strategies that emphasise community building and value alignment. To ensure a sustainable volunteering legacy, managers must implement di erentiated communication channels, such as digital platforms tailored to younger generations, to foster lasting engagement across diverse demographic groups. The multidisciplinary nature of sports events is also evident in how di erent stakeholders perceive quality. The case of GIMNASTRADA 2019, an international recreational gymnastics event, uses Service Quality Theory and Role Theory to demonstrate that "success" is highly subjective. The study found that the type of participation significantly influences quality ratings: while organisers and group leaders reported the highest levels of satisfaction, active gymnasts tended to have lower perceptions of service quality. This discrepancy is attributed to the "expectation-performance gap," in which active participants face greater performance pressure and have more stringent requirements for facilities and logistics. These findings suggest that sports management must move toward a tailored experience design, ensuring that the specific needs of athletes, families, and spectators are addressed separately to promote long-term loyalty and repeat participation. Sports events also serve as a "cultural battlefield" where national identity is constructed and contested. An analysis of Indonesian media narratives regarding the naturalisation of football players illustrates the tension between pragmatic nationalism and cultural essentialism. Media outlets often frame naturalised players as "national assets" who enhance international competitiveness, yet they simultaneously express scepticism about the athletes' "authenticity" and emotional ties to the nation. Drawing on the distinction between "thin citizenship" (legal recognition) and "thick citizenship" (cultural intimacy), the research shows how the media acts as a mediator of public perception. While some naturalised athletes successfully integrate by embracing local language and social initiatives, the discourse remains divided. This highlights the role of sporting events as critical sites for defining the symbolic boundaries of an "imagined community" in the era of globalised labour migration. From an economic and marketing perspective, the success of sports events is often linked to the "fit" or congruity between the event and its sponsoring brands. A metaanalytic review of 31 studies confirms that high levels of sports event-brand fit lead to positive cognitive, emotional, and behavioural responses from consumers. However, the e ectiveness of this fit is moderated by cultural contexts. In Eastern cultures, brand-event alignment is more e ective at generating emotional responses, reflecting a preference for harmony and collectivism. Conversely, in Western cultures, the fit has a stronger impact on behavioural intentions, such as purchase probability. Furthermore, the research suggests that symbolic brand responses-such as brand loyalty-are not instantaneous but require long-term sponsorship commitment and repeated interaction to bridge the "expectation gap" in consumers' minds. The final multidisciplinary lens focuses on the impact and legacy of sports events on the Quality of Life (QOL) of host communities. A scoping review of the literature indicates a significant shift from evaluating purely economic outcomes to measuring subjective well-being. While mega-events like the Olympics dominate the research, the review identifies an underexplored potential in small and mediumsized events to foster social capital and community cohesion. The findings suggest that the positive "feel-good" e ect of one-o mega-events is often temporary. In contrast, recurring participatory events (such as marathons) may o er more sustainable benefits for resident attachment and behavioural change. To advance this field, researchers advocate integrating objective measures, such as Heart Rate Variability (HRV), to complement subjective surveys and better understand the physiological mechanisms linking sports experiences to societal happiness.In conclusion, the articles in Exploring the Multidisciplinary Roles of Sports Events o er a profound and critical perspective on the role of sport in contemporary society. Collectively, they provide academics, event managers, and policymakers with practical insights and actionable tools to maximise the social legacies of sports events by understanding the intergenerational dynamics of volunteer motivation, improve service delivery through greater recognition of the role-specific expectations of diverse event participants, navigate the complex identity politics surrounding sports journalism and national team recruitment, optimise sponsorship strategies by acknowledging cultural di erences in consumer behaviour, and promote long-term societal well-being by moving beyond short-term economic metrics towards more holistic quality-of-life indicators. Taken together, the findings presented in this volume constitute a significant contribution to the ongoing dialogue on how sports events can be strategically leveraged to foster more inclusive, prosperous, and happier societies.

data.title: Effects of pacing strategy on performance and physiological responses in a simulated 1000-m kayak race under the new Olympic schedule
data.title_original: Effects of pacing strategy on performance and physiological responses in a simulated 1000-m kayak race under the new Olympic schedule
data.summary: Purpose: This study examined whether adding an all-out start (AO) to a self-paced strategy increased average power outputas a measure of performance in a fixed-duration 4-min kayak ergometer trial simulating a 1000-m kayak race under the newOlympic canoe sprint schedule, and whether this pacing modification altered physiological responses.Methods: Nine national-level male kayakers completed three 4-min kayak-ergometer trials over two consecutive days: a selfpaced (SP) trial on day 1, and even-paced (EP) and AO trials on day 2 separated by 2 hours to simulate semifinal and final,respectively. In EP, athletes matched the average power output (PO) from SP; in AO, they performed a 15-s maximal effortfollowed by self-paced paddling. Mechanical and physiological variables, including PO, stroke rate, oxygen uptake, heart rate(HR), blood lactate, and acid-base parameters, were measured. Data were analyzed with frequentist and Bayesian repeatedmeasures ANOVA.Results: Compared with SP, AO produced higher average PO (194 ± 14 vs 185 ± 22 W; P = .027; BF₁₀ = 1.82) and peak HR(195 ± 4 vs 192 ± 3 beats/min; P = .045; BF₁₀ = 4.22), although the HR difference lay within typical day-to-day variability.The remaining physiological variables did not differ between strategies (all P > .35), with Bayes factors (BF₁₀ = 0.25–0.43)providing anecdotal to moderate evidence for the null model.Conclusions: A 15-s all-out start superimposed on a self-paced strategy may increase average power output during a fixedduration 4-min kayak ergometer trial under the Olympic regatta schedule without increasing physiological strain. data.title: Infrastructure-Superstructure Contradictions in Vietnamese Elite Sports: An Analysis from the Perspective of Historical Materialism
data.title_original: Infrastructure-Superstructure Contradictions in Vietnamese Elite Sports: An Analysis from the Perspective of Historical Materialism
data.summary: Applying the historical materialist principle of the dialectical relationship between infrastructure and superstructure, this study examines the development of Vietnamese elite sports from 2011 to 2026. Using historical-logical analysis and an empirical survey of managers, coaches, and athletes, the study identifies a performance paradox: Vietnam has maintained strong results at the SEA Games while achieving more limited outcomes at the ASIAD and Olympic levels. The analysis associates this pattern with institutional desynchronization between changing economic and material conditions and slower administrative and regulatory adaptation. Key issues include barriers to public-private partnerships, limited autonomy of sports federations, shortcomings in athlete remuneration and occupational insurance, and insufficient investment in advanced training technologies. In relation to Decision No. 1189/QD-TTg and national sports development objectives to 2030 with a vision to 2045, the study proposes coordinated institutional reforms, improved resource mobilization, and greater application of artificial intelligence, biosensors, and sports biomedicine to support sustainable elite sports development.

data.title: 33rd SEA Games Takeaways: Balancing Sport and Southeast Asia’s Complex Environment
data.title_original: 33rd SEA Games Takeaways: Balancing Sport and Southeast Asia’s Complex Environment
data.summary: The SEA Games this year took place in Thailand, marking the seventh time that the country has hosted Southeast Asia's biggest sporting event. Thailand comes out on top of the table, achieving an all-time record of 233 out of 573 possible Gold Medals, overtaking Vietnam's 2022 record of 205 Gold Medals. Another interesting fact regarding this year's event is that several countries sent their largest-ever delegations to the 33rd SEA Games as Singapore sent 930, the Philippines with 1,168, and Malaysia with 1,166 athletes, positively reflecting the expanded 50-sport program and Olympic-aligned events in this year's SEA Games. Despite the positive updates from the 33rd SEA Games, the event also saw Cambodia withdraw 1,515 athletes due to the intensifying Cambodian-Thai border conflict, leaving only 10 countries participating. In this sense, the event mirrored broader ASEAN challenges in managing intra-regional disputes while upholding the principle of regional harmony. A setback also occurred during the preparation, as cyclone Senyar hit and caused flooding in the Songkhla province, forcing 10 sports to relocate from the Southern venue just a week before the opening on 9th December 2025. Some technical issues by the organiser also coloured this year's event, including flag and national anthem errors, which raised questions about the host's preparedness. data.title: Sport Motivation Among Young Fencers Training in a Ukrainian Olympic Reserve School During Wartime: An Exploratory Cross-Sectional Study
data.title_original: Sport Motivation Among Young Fencers Training in a Ukrainian Olympic Reserve School During Wartime: An Exploratory Cross-Sectional Study
data.summary: Background and purpose Young athletes in Ukraine continue to train during the war, which may disrupt training routines and affect their motivation. However, evidence on sport motivation among young athletes training in Olympic reserve systems during wartime remains limited. This study examined motivation among young fencers training in a Ukrainian Olympic reserve school during wartime and its associations with perceived coach support and war-related disruption of training. Material and methods This exploratory cross-sectional study involved 64 young fencers from a Specialized Youth Sports School of Olympic Reserve in Mykolaiv, Ukraine. Participants ranged in age from 10 to 19 years (M = 14.81, SD = 2.05). Sport motivation was assessed using the Sport Motivation Scale-II, which measures intrinsic motivation, integrated regulation, identified regulation, introjected regulation, external regulation, and amotivation. Additional study-specific items assessed war-related disruption of training and perceived coach support. Descriptive statistics, Cronbach’s alpha coefficients, Pearson correlation analysis, independent samples t-tests, and one-way analysis of variance were used. Results The highest mean scores were observed for identified regulation, intrinsic motivation, and integrated regulation, whereas external regulation and amotivation showed lower values. These three dimensions showed acceptable-to-good internal consistency and moderate-to-strong positive correlations with each other. No statistically significant associations were found between motivational dimensions and perceived war-related disruption or coach support. Female athletes reported significantly higher intrinsic motivation than male athletes (p = 0.010), while no other gender differences were observed. Competition participation level was significantly associated only with introjected regulation (F(2, 61) = 3.45, p = 0.038, η² = 0.10), with athletes without competition experience reporting higher scores than those competing at national or international levels. Conclusions More self-determined forms of motivation predominated among young fencers training in a Ukrainian Olympic reserve school during wartime. Identified regulation, intrinsic motivation, and integrated regulation were also the most closely related motivational dimensions. Perceived war-related disruption and coach support were not significantly associated with motivational dimensions. The small single-school sample limits the generalizability of these findings, and larger studies are needed to confirm them.

data.title_original: Sports morale in post-existentialist concept of ‘sociocultural phenomenon’
data.summary: You are trying to identify the philosophical and ideological orientation of the conceptual development of the theory of sports ethics as a specific form of social consciousness. Sports ethics is a kind of universal morality based on the specifics of a professional sports activity, which represents a complex internal system of interpersonal relations, as well as the external structure of the relationship of athletes in various cultures of society. This involves internalization of the athletes and sports managers traditions and norms of social behavior and attitudes inherent to the subculture of public, political and social organizations. Sport not only reflects the morality of public moral and ethical standards, and manifests its own principles and the relationship between athletes as normative behavior in globalizovanom world. From the point of view of the morality of the body, which is experiencing a variety of internal suffering from immense desires of the soul, in sports and sports physical activity due to moral imperatives are allowed to conflict of body and soul.

data.summary: The phenomenological reduction of sport and physical and sport activities is conducted in the article to determine its semantic relevance in the history of cultural and historical practices. A comparative analysis reveals development of myth, philosophy and religion perspectives for sport, which is transformed from leisure and quite sophisticated form of human activity into the sphere of social life. Historically, sport articulated the strength and beauty of sound psychosomatic human body. Sport in nowadays mosaic cultural environment is considered to be a stabilizer in preserving human creative nature and the cultural lever which serves as an axis for its diversity. It is stated in the article findings that in today’s diverse dimensions of sports existence, in particular with regard to its objectivity, communicability, individualization, etc., the previous societal cultural and civilization experience in keeping and improving the physicality is at focus, which creates the need for philosophical reflection on its relevance.

data.title_original: Peer Review Report for Preprint: Мировоззренческие основания холистического коучинга тренера-философа Перси Уэллса Черутти. Часть первая
data.summary: Мировоззренческие основания холистического коучинга тренера-философа Перси Уэллса Черутти.Часть первая Всегда следует помнить, что Перси был не просто тренером по легкой атлетике; он был философом и поэтом, который вдохновлял спортсменов полностью раскрыть свой потенциал.Л. Майерс Перси Уэллс Черутти (1895-1975) -австралийский тренер, подготовивший около тридцати мировых рекордсменов в разных видах спорта, включая олимпийского чемпиона Герберта Джеймса Эллиота.П. Черутти относился к редкому типу тренеров-философов, считавшим мировоззренческую подготовку спортсменов важной составляющей их личностного и атлетического развития.Объектом исследования являются тексты П. Черутти и научные труды, посвященные его жизни и тренерской деятельности.Цель работы -выявление мировоззренческих оснований холистического коучинга П. Черутти, направленного на всестороннее совершенствование спортсмена.К задачам первой части исследования относятся: 1) определение основных событий жизни П. Черутти, существенно повлиявших на формирование его мировоззрения и рассмотренных в контексте социальных процессов современного ему австралийского общества; 2) выявление философско-религиозных и спортивных авторитетов австралийского тренера; 3) экспликация составляющих натуралистического компонента мировоззрения П. Черутти.Методология исследования базируется на социокультурном и герменевтическом подходах с использованием познавательных процедур категоризации и анализа, а также дескриптивного и исторического методов.Научная новизна исследования заключается в целостном обзоре философских взглядов П. Черутти.Выводы работы обусловлены решением поставленных в ней задач.«Путеводными звездами» П. Черутти были философско-религиозные и спортивные авторитеты.К первой группе относились психофизические практики йоги, воззрения Джидду Кришнамурти и Сократа.На основе идей стоиков, спартанцев и Леонардо да Винчи он разработал свое учение о «стотанах» и «универсалах» как выразителях лучших для спорта качеств и направленной к эвдемонии жизни.Христос и Франциск Ассизский привлекали П. Черутти своим опытом спасения и очищения через боль.К спортивным авторитетам П. Черутти относятся Артур Ньютон, Георг Гаккеншмидт и Боб Хоффман, которых можно рассматривать как предтеч холистического коучинга.Основа мировоззрения П. Черутти -натурализм и гуманизм.Он рассматривал природу как выражение божества, тренировочную площадку, учителя правильного образа жизни и бега, а также целителя.П. Черутти обосновывал важность для выживания человека и спортивных достижений инстинктивной сферы его психики и стал пионером исследований экологической составляющей и гуманистического потенциала беговой активности в природной среде.тренер (coach) Ключевое слово: мировоззрение (worldview) Ключевое слово: стотан (stotan) Ключевое слово:

data.title: Мировоззренческие основания холистического коучинга тренера-философа Перси Уэллса Черутти. Часть первая
data.title_original: Мировоззренческие основания холистического коучинга тренера-философа Перси Уэллса Черутти. Часть первая
data.summary: Перси Уэллс Черутти (1895-1975) – австралийский тренер, подготовивший около тридцати мировых рекордсменов в разных видах спорта, включая олимпийского чемпиона Герберта Джеймса Эллиота. П. Черутти относился к редкому типу тренеров-философов, считавшим мировоззренческую подготовку спортсменов важной составляющей их личностного и атлетического развития. Объектом исследования являются тексты П. Черутти и научные труды, посвященные его жизни и тренерской деятельности. Цель работы ‒ выявление мировоззренческих оснований холистического коучинга П. Черутти, направленного на всестороннее совершенствование спортсмена. К задачам первой части исследования относятся: 1) определение основных событий жизни П. Черутти, существенно повлиявших на формирование его мировоззрения и рассмотренных в контексте социальных процессов современного ему австралийского общества; 2) выявление философско-религиозных и спортивных авторитетов австралийского тренера; 3) экспликация составляющих натуралистического компонента мировоззрения П. Черутти. Методология исследования базируется на социокультурном и герменевтическом подходах с использованием познавательных процедур категоризации и анализа, а также дескриптивного и исторического методов. Научная новизна исследования заключается в целостном обзоре философских взглядов П. Черутти. Выводы работы обусловлены решением поставленных в ней задач. «Путеводными звездами» П. Черутти были философско-религиозные и спортивные авторитеты. К первой группе относились психофизические практики йоги, воззрения Джидду Кришнамурти и Сократа. На основе идей стоиков, спартанцев и Леонардо да Винчи он разработал свое учение о «стотанах» и «универсалах» как выразителях лучших для спорта качеств и направленной к эвдемонии жизни. Христос и Франциск Ассизский привлекали П. Черутти своим опытом спасения и очищения через боль. К спортивным авторитетам П. Черутти относятся Артур Ньютон, Георг Гаккеншмидт и Боб Хоффман, которых можно рассматривать как предтеч холистического коучинга. Основа мировоззрения П. Черутти ‒ натурализм и гуманизм. Он рассматривал природу как выражение божества, тренировочную площадку, учителя правильного образа жизни и бега, а также целителя. П. Черутти обосновывал важность для выживания человека и спортивных достижений инстинктивной сферы его психики и стал пионером исследований экологической составляющей и гуманистического потенциала беговой активности в природной среде.

Черутти были философско-религиозные и спортивные авторитеты. К первой группе относились психофизические практики йоги, воззрения Джидду Кришнамурти и Сократа. Черутти относятся Артур Ньютон, Георг Гаккеншмидт и Боб Хоффман, которых можно рассматривать как предтеч холистического коучинга. Основа мировоззрения П. Черутти ‒ натурализм и гуманизм. Черутти обосновывал важность для выживания человека и спортивных достижений инстинктивной сферы его психики и стал пионером исследований экологической составляющей и гуманистического потенциала беговой активности в природной среде.

data.title: The pedagogical system of Percy Cerutty's holistic coaching
data.title_original: The pedagogical system of Percy Cerutty's holistic coaching
data.summary: The objective of this article is to identify and systematize the didactic principles of Australian coach Percy Cerutty’s “holistic coaching,” to analyze the mechanisms of their implementation through the case study of Olympic champion Herb Elliott, and to provide a critical evaluation of this methodology. The study is based on a theoretical synthesis of scientific and methodological literature, an analysis of original English-language primary sources previously untranslated into Russian (Cerutty’s three most well-known books and Elliott’s autobiography), and a historical and pedagogical comparison of training management systems. The research establishes that Cerutty’s pedagogical paradigm is fundamentally based on the rejection of the strict mathematical regulation of training loads. Four fundamental principles of his system have been identified: the intellectualization of training; the cultivation of lactate tolerance through asceticism (the "Stotan" code, combining Stoic inner discipline with Spartan endurance); the delegation of responsibility to the athlete (fostering proprioception rather than stopwatch-based control); and the utilization of a nature-centric training environment. Using Elliott’s case, it is demonstrated that shifting the focus toward internal volitional self-regulation facilitated not only outstanding competitive results but also the athlete’s successful transition into academic and business environments. The article examines the specific reception of the Australian coach’s ideas within Russian sports theory: namely, the classic school of periodization’s rejection of his intuitive approach, despite the simultaneous and successful assimilation of his specific training methods. Critical vulnerabilities of Cerutty’s system are also exposed, including anti-scientism, the uncontrolled risk of overtraining, and the latent authoritarianism inherent in the "coach-guru" model. Cerutty’s historical legacy demonstrates that shifting away from perceiving the athlete as a mere biomechanical object in favor of a subject-to-subject interaction expands the organism's adaptive reserves. Integrating elements of intuitive control and psychological recovery into modern training plans can significantly reduce the risks of early burnout and sports maladaptation among Olympic reserve athletes.

data.title: DEVELOPMENT OF SELECTION CRITERIA FOR TREE AND SHRUB SPECIES FOR LANDSCAPING OLYMPIC PARKS UNDER HUMID SUBTROPICAL CLIMATE CONDITIONS (USING THE OLYMPIC PARK AS AN EXAMPLE)
data.title_original: DEVELOPMENT OF SELECTION CRITERIA FOR TREE AND SHRUB SPECIES FOR LANDSCAPING OLYMPIC PARKS UNDER HUMID SUBTROPICAL CLIMATE CONDITIONS (USING THE OLYMPIC PARK AS AN EXAMPLE)
data.summary: The article presents a system of criteria for selecting tree and shrub plants for landscaping Olympic parks in humid subtropical conditions using the Olympic Park in Sochi as a case study. Based on an analysis of regulatory documents (Ministry of Natural Resources of Russia, 2011; SanPiN 1567-76; ITF, 2020) and scientific literature, a hierarchical system of 5 groups of criteria (functional–operational, ecological, phytosanitary, architectural–decorative, agrotechnical) was developed, with weighting coefficients determined by the pairwise comparison method. Mandatory restrictions on allergenicity, injury hazard, invasiveness, shading, and leaf fall were established. A point scale (0–3) for 22 parameters and a formula for calculating the integral score I (0–100) were proposed. The methodology was tested on 25 species recommended by the Nikitsky Botanical Garden. The highest scores (≥90) were obtained by Sabal palmetta (95.8), Cupressus sempervirens (91.4), and Olea europaea (90.2). Species with I < 60 (plane tree, birch, walnut) were excluded from the assortment for high traffic areas. A flowchart of the restriction checking algorithm and a diagram for calculating shade zones were developed. The proposed methodology can be used for landscaping design of Olympic and other major sports facilities in subtropical regions.

data.title: Olympic show: media and national identity in Jonathan Coe’s novel “Middle England” (2018)
data.title_original: Olympic show: media and national identity in Jonathan Coe’s novel “Middle England” (2018)
data.summary: This article examines Jonathan Coe’s novel “Middle England” (2018) as a significant phenomenon within Brexlit (Brexit literature). The analysis focuses on Chapter 15, which stands in deliberate contrast to the remainder of the novel. This retrospective episode, centered on the televised broadcast of the 2012 London Olympics opening ceremony, portrays the final “happy spectacle” of national unity. Drawing on Benedict Anderson’s concept of the “imagined community”, the study analyzes how Danny Boyle’s directorial vision constructs a narrative of national identity grounded in ideals of progress and collective solidarity, while acknowledging diverse social and cultural identities. The article discusses the historicalcultural context, Coe’s preoccupation with media power, and the shared artistic strategies of Boyle and Coe (montage, counterpoint, allusiveness, immersive effects, multi-perspectival narration, and panoramic scope) as expressions of Christopher Hill’s notion of “radical patriotism”. A comparative analysis of Coe’s literary technique with Boyle’s television show and W. P. Frith’s Victorian genre painting reveals the “mirror of society” effect. The research contributes to scholarly debates on the construction of collective identity and highlights Coe’s self-reflexive stance as an author. Ultimately, “Middle England” operates as a satirical “state-of-the-nation” novel that rejects both the traditional Victorian resolution of class conflict and the seductive media illusion of national unity, offering instead a bitterly realistic depiction of the collapse of Britain’s social institutions and the very ideal of national identity.
